sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 3946.7 ± 327.8 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Anti-FLAG immunofluorescence confirmed both total and cell-surface expression of the FLAG-tagged NPBWR1 construct (L2); TANGO beta-arrestin recruitment assay is the functional readout of the platform but NPBWR1-specific functional data are not individually reported in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: NPBWR1 is a GPCR with no endogenous signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–37 as extracellular and residues 311–328 as intracellular, leaving the N-terminus as the sole extracellular terminus. The PRESTO-TANGO construct prepends an artificial SP and FLAG before residue M1, so after SP cleavage the FLAG sits immediately N-terminal to M1 (insert_after_residue = 0, residue_after = M). The N-terminal extracellular domain spans 37 residues before TM1 (which begins at V38), providing ample space for a ~15–20 aa tag well clear of the TM boundary. PRESTO-TANGO platform (Kroeze et al., PMC4424118): an artificial cleavable signal sequence was prepended to NPBWR1/GPR7 followed by a FLAG epitope tag to drive membrane localization and enable surface detection; after signal-peptide cleavage the FLAG is displayed at the extracellular N-terminus of the full-length, membrane-anchored receptor.

sources.claim: At the 5′-end, we included a cleavable signal sequence to promote membrane localization 23 and a FLAG epitope tag in order to be able to monitor cell surface expression by immunohistochemistry.

literature_notes: Only two ledger lines are available (L1, L2), both from the same PRESTO-TANGO paper (PMC4424118) and both describing the same N-terminal FLAG construct. No ledger evidence supports any insertion in ECL1 (96–110), ECL2 (178–201), or ECL3 (274–286). The C-terminus (311–328) is intracellular and therefore not a surface-tag site. L2 was used to confirm surface expression but L1 is the primary clip pinning the tag position.
